    Subgroup meta-analysis

    Source: R/meta-regression.R
    meta_subgroup.Rd

    meta_subgroup() pools effect sizes within the levels of a categorical variable and tests whether the subgroup estimates differ.

    Usage

    meta_subgroup(
  .data,
  group,
  yi = .yi,
  vi = .vi,
  method = "REML",
  test = "z",
  level = 0.95,
  study = NULL,
  tau2 = c("separate", "common")
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A <meta_es> from meta_effect_size() or any data frame with effect sizes and sampling variances.

    group

    <data-masking> The grouping variable.

    yi, vi

    <data-masking> Columns holding the effect sizes and sampling variances. Default to .yi and .vi.

    method

    Estimator of the between-study variance: "REML", "ML", "DL", "PM", "SJ" or "FE" (common effect).

    test

    "z" for normal based inference or "hksj" for the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment.

    level

    Confidence level for intervals.

    study

    <data-masking> Optional study labels. Taken from the <meta_es> when available.

    tau2

    "separate" or "common" between-study variance.

    Value

    A <meta_fit> with one row per subgroup, including the number of studies (k), tau2 and I2 of each subgroup. The test of subgroup differences is returned by glance().

    Details

    With tau2 = "separate" (the default) each subgroup is pooled on its own, with its own \(\tau^2\), and the test of subgroup differences is the Q statistic of a common-effect meta-analysis of the subgroup estimates (Borenstein et al., 2009). With tau2 = "common" a single \(\tau^2\) is assumed and the subgroup means are estimated by a meta-regression without an intercept; the test of differences is then a Wald test (or an F test with test = "hksj") that all subgroup means are equal.

    References

    Borenstein, M., Hedges, L. V., Higgins, J. P. T. and Rothstein, H. R. (2009). Introduction to Meta-Analysis, chapter 19. Wiley.

    Examples

    bcg <- meta_effect_size(bcg_trials, "RR",
  event1 = tpos, n1 = tpos + tneg, event2 = cpos, n2 = cpos + cneg
)
meta_subgroup(bcg, alloc)
#> # Subgroup meta-analysis <meta_fit>
#> # Model: random effects, restricted maximum likelihood
#> # Measure: log risk ratio; k = 13
#> # Q(10) = 132.37, p < 0.0001
#> # Test of subgroup differences: Q(2) = 1.86, p = 0.3943
#> # A tibble: 3 × 10
#>   term       estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high     k  tau2
#>   <chr>         <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <int> <dbl>
#> 1 alternate    -0.541     0.282     -1.92 5.48e-2    -1.09    0.0111     2 0.133
#> 2 random       -0.971     0.276     -3.52 4.34e-4    -1.51   -0.430      7 0.393
#> 3 systematic   -0.424     0.360     -1.18 2.38e-1    -1.13    0.281      4 0.400
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: I2 <dbl>
meta_subgroup(bcg, alloc, tau2 = "common") |> glance()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 25
#>   model_type  nobs method test   tau2 tau2.low tau2.high   tau    I2    H2    R2
#>   <chr>      <int> <chr>  <chr> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 subgroup      13 REML   z     0.362    0.124      1.19 0.601  88.8  8.91    NA
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: QE <dbl>, df.residual <int>, p.QE <dbl>, QM <dbl>,
#> #   p.QM <dbl>, pred.low <dbl>, pred.high <dbl>, logLik <dbl>, AIC <dbl>,
#> #   BIC <dbl>, Q.between <dbl>, df.between <int>, p.between <dbl>,
#> #   tau2_type <chr>
